item.title: Val d'Oust Cultural Center / Atelier 56S
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The Val d'Oust Cultural Center stands as a key public facility at the intersection of the church square, Jules Ferry Street, and the landscaped public garden. The project forms part of a broader strategy to enhance public spaces and strengthen pedestrian connections throughout the town.

item.title: Has Architecture Ever Been Entirely Human? Beatriz Colomina and Mark Wigley on the Microbial Nature of Architecture
item.dc:creator: Christele Harrouk
item.description: Architecture has long been understood as a discipline created by humans and for humans. But in We the Bacteria: Notes Toward Biotic Architecture, Beatriz Colomina and Mark Wigley challenge that assumption, arguing that "microbes invented architecture." From this premise unfolds an alternative history of architecture that shifts the focus away from human exceptionalism and toward the microorganisms that have shaped life, environments, and the built world for billions of years.

item.title: Rooms That Appear: Sliding Partitions and Conditional Domestic Space
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Yeung
item.description: Sliding doors are often discussed through efficiency. They save the swing radius of a conventional door, allow compact rooms to function more easily, and help small apartments borrow a few extra centimeters of usable space. Yet in many interiors, their more interesting role is not only spatial economy. Sliding partitions transform the reading of the room itself. A bedroom, study, guest room, dining area, or workspace can appear when a panel is closed, disappear when it is opened, and remain ambiguous when the boundary is translucent or partial.

item.title: Chengdu Pavilion / IwamotoScott Architecture
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: The Chengdu pavilion was commissioned as an exhibition pavilion with a project brief seeking a decidedly future-forward design. It serves both as an iconic symbol of the ethos and purpose of the adjacent future-facing urban expansion currently underway and as an information center for the public to learn about this large new master-planned district called the Chengdu Future Science and Technology City now in development and construction in the Sichuan Province.

item.title: MAD’s Shenzhen Bay Culture Square and Dorte Mandrup’s PLACE Exhibition: This Week’s Review
item.dc:creator: Reyyan Dogan
item.description: This week, architecture's relationship with culture took center stage through exhibitions, public projects, and new cultural infrastructure that extend architectural discourse beyond the building itself. While major exhibitions from Australia, Shanghai, Barcelona, and Copenhagen examined themes of housing, landscape, and place through research and design, newly unveiled projects in China and Italy demonstrate how museums, performance venues, and mixed-use projects are increasingly conceived as open public landscapes rather than isolated institutions, while new exhibitions and construction milestones reflect ongoing experimentation in adaptive reuse, context-responsive design, and flexible urban environments.

item.title: Masseria Ficazzella / Valari Studio
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: Nestled in the Fasano countryside among olive trees and distant views of the Adriatic, Masseria Ficazzella is a restoration by Valari Studio that reimagines a historic Puglian farmhouse as a contemporary private home. Designed for a young, non-Italian family, the project balances architectural authenticity, domestic comfort, and a close relationship with the landscape.

item.title: Grand Paris Express Advances Urban Renewal Through 68 Architect-Designed Stations
item.dc:creator: Antonia Piñeiro
item.description: The Grand Paris Express project consists of 200 kilometers of new, fully automated metro lines, 68 new stations, and four new orbital lines (15, 16, 17, and 18), in addition to the extension of Line 14. The network is being delivered in phases between 2024 and 2031: Line 14's 8 stations are fully operational following its 2024 extension, Line 18 is the most advanced of the new lines, with testing underway ahead of its first opening, and civil engineering is largely complete on many sections, with tracks, systems, architectural fit-out, and testing now progressing station by station. Each of the 68 stations is assigned to a specific architect or architectural team, sometimes in collaboration with landscape architects for above-ground elements.

item.title: Workmanship and Imperfection: 10 Projects Between Hand and Machine
item.dc:creator: Diogo Borges Ferreira
item.description: In 1968, the furniture designer and RCA professor David Pye published The Nature and Art of Workmanship, a book built around a distinction between "workmanship of risk" and the "workmanship of certainty." Pye was not writing about architecture, and despite how the phrase gets used today, he was not really writing about hands versus machines either. He pointed out that a printing press, entirely mechanical, still depends on someone judging the ink and the register, while a woodturner working a lathe by hand can follow a template closely enough that almost nothing is left to chance.

item.title: The Plinth House / Cambra Buró
item.dc:creator: Miwa Negoro
item.description: The Plinth House is a 3,000 sqm private villa on the coast of Abu Alhusaniya, Kuwait, completed in 2025. Designed by Cambra Buró under a full architectural, interior, and landscape scope, the house is structured as a dialogue between restraint and expression: a sculpted travertine plinth anchors the building to the ground, while a minimal, calm upper volume rests above it, deliberately understated in contrast to the base.

item.title: Entwined Wall Residence / IGArchitects
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: This project is the renovation of a single floor within a commercial tenant building into a restaurant. Rather than dividing the program into a conventional relationship of front-of-house and back-of-house, the design explores how the various functions of the restaurant can be encompassed and gently interconnected through a single continuous wall.

item.title: aa Market / Vari Architects
item.dc:creator: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang
item.description: aa market is a rooftop lifestyle market initiated, designed, and operated by vari architects in Chongqing. Rather than beginning as a conventional commercial commission, the project grew out of the architects' own daily needs. Located above their studio, it was first imagined as a place where the team, friends, and the surrounding community could eat, drink tea, meet, pause, and spend time together. From this small-scale spatial practice, the project gradually developed into an attempt to reactivate an overlooked rooftop within an industrial park and transform it into a new public interface for everyday urban life.

item.title: Brutalist Penthouse / Barde + vanVoltt
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: Located in the Escandón neighborhood of Mexico City, this 300-square-meter penthouse renovation by Barde vanVoltt reinterprets brutalist architecture through warmth, craftsmanship, and domestic comfort. Designed for two creative professionals, the project transforms an existing rooftop apartment into a calm sanctuary above one of the city's most vibrant districts.

item.title: Praça House / Felipe Hess Arquitetos
item.dc:creator: Andreas Luco
item.description: Implanted on a narrow and deep plot of 10 x 60 meters in Jardim Paulistano, Casa Praça is organized into three blocks interspersed with patios. This configuration takes advantage of the lot's geometry to distribute the spaces functionally and create open areas that enhance the entry of natural light and encourage social interaction.

item.title: PH Juana / Estudio NU
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: PH Juana proposes a space where the existing and the new coexist to give rise to a fresh reinterpretation of contemporary living.

item.title: HD House / Desvão Atelier
item.dc:creator: Pilar Caballero
item.description: Casa HD is located within a residential enclave between Sesimbra and the village of Azeitão, occupying a trapezoidal plot bounded by the access road to the east and adjacent buildings to the north and south. While the topography is relatively gentle, the existing slope was leveraged to raise the construction one metre above street level, eliminating the need for major earthworks and enhancing visual and spatial autonomy. Situated near the Arrábida Natural Park, the site benefits from a striking natural backdrop dominated by the surrounding mountain range. The landscape is characterized by cork oaks, holm oaks, and scattered low vegetation, typical of the Portuguese montado ecosystem.

item.title: Paraiso Remodel / Austin Sandy Architects
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: The Paraiso Remodel transforms a ranch house in a hilly East Bay neighborhood into a light-filled family home. Originally a T-shaped structure with a piecemeal 1960s addition, the house had grown dark and chopped up over the years, prompting its new owners to turn to Austin Sandy for a rethink.

item.title: RDH House / Čechvala Architects
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The site sits in Bratislava's Sihoť district along Devínska Road, at a rare meeting point of two contrasting landscapes: the wooded rise of the Carpathian massif on one side and a quiet arm of the Danube on the other. The house also stands close to a well-known horticultural center, giving the plot a prominent presence within the neighborhood.

item.description:

The International Sustainable Building Competition will be held at COP31 and will be open to participants from all countries, with the aim to promote energy-efficient, low-carbon, climate-resilient, and sustainable building practices, highlight best solutions, and support their global dissemination.

item.title: Futurebuild Queensland
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: Futurebuild Queensland is the state's only dedicated trade exhibition for the building, design and development sectors. Held annually, it brings together the entire state’s design and build ecosystem for two days of product discovery, industry connection and business opportunities that help shape how Queensland builds.

item.title: La Feria De Diseño Medellín
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
La Feria De Diseño Medellín powered by idd cologne is a professional platform connecting Latin American design with international markets.

From September 10–12, 2026, the event will bring together brands, architects, interior designers, buyers, developers, distributors and industry leaders at Plaza Mayor Medellín.

Its exhibition and business agenda covers furniture, lighting, kitchens, architecture, interior design, wellness and décor, creating new opportunities across Latin America and the Caribbean.

item.title: Escaping Demolition: The Preservation of the A. Conger Goodyear House
item.dc:creator: Agustina Iñiguez
item.description: As pillars of our cultural landscape, many masterpieces of the Modern Movement are often demolished, abandoned, or altered regardless of the context in which they are located. Preserving this architectural legacy highlights the role of architecture and design professionals in shaping built environments where continuity between the past and the present reinforces communities' sense of place. On Long Island, a coalition of advocates came together to save the A. Conger Goodyear House, which dates to 1938 and was designed by Edward Durell Stone. Considered one of the notable examples of the International Style in the United States, the house attracted significant attention throughout the 1940s, appearing in specialized journals, books, and popular publications.

item.title: UCAD Dakar Student Housing / Hardel Le Bihan Architectes
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: Since 2015, in response to growing demand and to improve living conditions on the campus of Cheikh Anta Diop University, the Senegalese state has relied on AMSA Realty SA (the real-estate arm of the insurer AMSA) to develop around ten residences and house an additional 10,000 students in the UCAD and Claudel sectors. From the outset, project management was entrusted to the REDMAN group and its local agency, while architectural design was assigned to HARDEL LE BIHAN ARCHITECTES, in collaboration with Dakar-based ALUN BE and landscape studio Niez Studio.

item.title: Buildner's 3rd Architect's Stair Competition Winners Explore the Stair as a Form of Architectural Expression
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: Buildner has announced the results of its third edition Architect's Stair international architecture ideas competition. The event invited designers to reflect on one of architecture's oldest and most symbolic elements: the stair. Beyond its functional role as a connector of levels, the stair was positioned here as a medium of architectural storytelling—an invitation to explore ideas of procession, sequence, space, and form.
